title: CS-P32768: fixed plateaus improve classical memory with unchanged other envelopes

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and secret s modulo N, n=ceil(log2N), the single CS-P32768 algorithm in proof.md (finite exhaustive branch n<2^48; otherwise r=ceil(sqrt n), H=floor(839r/1000), dl=ceil(6759r/10000), Qtarget=ceil(1599r/1600), A=H-dl, L4=ceil((Qtarget-A)/2), Mmax=A+L4, hmax=A+2L4, kappa=ceil(log2Mmax)+3, minimal mixed-tree prefixes with binary input widths dl+i and quartic widths H-floor(j/32768), aux=H+1+2j and full four-input windows, Kc=8192(2r+u+30), Kp=8192(u+100), u=ceil(log2n), full-label implicit-fiber implementation, coarse-cost mixed-arity exponential-demand cutoffs, bounded odd bootstrap, signed near-parity votes and smaller two-adic root budgets) recovers the entire secret with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8. On every branch total charged work is O(n^3 log2(n)2^((67011/40000)sqrt n)), with stronger main-branch bound O(n^3 log2(n)2^(hmax+dl)). All gates, bit sorting/listing, scan lookups, addresses, source costs, initialization, failed attempts, discards and resets are included. Its exact growth index is1/2, jointly with the other claims. For n=1 logarithmic envelopes use their positive values at n=2, without changing the structured asymptotic forms.

For every N>=2 and secret s modulo N, n=ceil(log2N), the single CS-P32768 algorithm in proof.md (finite exhaustive branch n<2^48; otherwise r=ceil(sqrt n), H=floor(839r/1000), dl=ceil(6759r/10000), Qtarget=ceil(1599r/1600), A=H-dl, L4=ceil((Qtarget-A)/2), Mmax=A+L4, hmax=A+2L4, kappa=ceil(log2Mmax)+3, minimal mixed-tree prefixes with binary input widths dl+i and quartic widths H-floor(j/32768), aux=H+1+2j and full four-input windows, Kc=8192(2r+u+30), Kp=8192(u+100), u=ceil(log2n), full-label implicit-fiber implementation, coarse-cost mixed-arity exponential-demand cutoffs, bounded odd bootstrap, signed near-parity votes and smaller two-adic root budgets) recovers the entire secret with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8. On every branch peak classical workspace is O(n2^((839/1000)sqrt n)) bits, with stronger main-branch bound O(n2^H), including all retained full-label tables, heap/list/rank/tuple scratch, counter and decoder records. Its exact growth index is1/2, jointly with the other claims. For n=1 logarithmic envelopes use their positive values at n=2, without changing the structured asymptotic forms.

For every N>=2 and secret s modulo N, n=ceil(log2N), the single CS-P32768 algorithm in proof.md (finite exhaustive branch n<2^48; otherwise r=ceil(sqrt n), H=floor(839r/1000), dl=ceil(6759r/10000), Qtarget=ceil(1599r/1600), A=H-dl, L4=ceil((Qtarget-A)/2), Mmax=A+L4, hmax=A+2L4, kappa=ceil(log2Mmax)+3, minimal mixed-tree prefixes with binary input widths dl+i and quartic widths H-floor(j/32768), aux=H+1+2j and full four-input windows, Kc=8192(2r+u+30), Kp=8192(u+100), u=ceil(log2n), full-label implicit-fiber implementation, coarse-cost mixed-arity exponential-demand cutoffs, bounded odd bootstrap, signed near-parity votes and smaller two-adic root budgets) recovers the entire secret with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8. On every branch peak accessible quantum workspace is O(n), including the full mixed depth-first stack, source/data, modular/extractor and lookup scratch, roots and reset wires. No QRAM or coherent bank is used. Its exact growth index is0, jointly with the other claims. For n=1 logarithmic envelopes use their positive values at n=2, without changing the structured asymptotic forms.

For every N>=2 and secret s modulo N, n=ceil(log2N), the single CS-P32768 algorithm in proof.md (finite exhaustive branch n<2^48; otherwise r=ceil(sqrt n), H=floor(839r/1000), dl=ceil(6759r/10000), Qtarget=ceil(1599r/1600), A=H-dl, L4=ceil((Qtarget-A)/2), Mmax=A+L4, hmax=A+2L4, kappa=ceil(log2Mmax)+3, minimal mixed-tree prefixes with binary input widths dl+i and quartic widths H-floor(j/32768), aux=H+1+2j and full four-input windows, Kc=8192(2r+u+30), Kp=8192(u+100), u=ceil(log2n), full-label implicit-fiber implementation, coarse-cost mixed-arity exponential-demand cutoffs, bounded odd bootstrap, signed near-parity votes and smaller two-adic root budgets) recovers the entire secret with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8. On every branch total acquired source copies are O(n^(3/2)log2(n)2^((1599/1600)sqrt n)), including rejected labels, failed inputs and aborted work. Main-branch exact cap is Q<=(Y+6)Ccap+2nCf+Kp, with D_R=8*dl*2^hmax*(R+u+16), C_R=4*D_R, Ccap=C_Kc, Cf=C_Kp, Y=ceil(log2Ccap). Finite exhaustive recovery acquires at most N(n+10) copies and is included through absolute outer constants; no main cap is asserted there. Its exact growth index is1/2, jointly with the other claims. For n=1 logarithmic envelopes use their positive values at n=2, without changing the structured asymptotic forms.

For every N>=2 and secret s modulo N, n=ceil(log2N), the single CS-P32768 algorithm in proof.md (finite exhaustive branch n<2^48; otherwise r=ceil(sqrt n), H=floor(839r/1000), dl=ceil(6759r/10000), Qtarget=ceil(1599r/1600), A=H-dl, L4=ceil((Qtarget-A)/2), Mmax=A+L4, hmax=A+2L4, kappa=ceil(log2Mmax)+3, minimal mixed-tree prefixes with binary input widths dl+i and quartic widths H-floor(j/32768), aux=H+1+2j and full four-input windows, Kc=8192(2r+u+30), Kp=8192(u+100), u=ceil(log2n), full-label implicit-fiber implementation, coarse-cost mixed-arity exponential-demand cutoffs, bounded odd bootstrap, signed near-parity votes and smaller two-adic root budgets) recovers the entire secret with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8. The proved malformed fraction is epsilon(n)=0 under independent ideal source copies. The same whole-secret success and four joint bounds apply under this promise. No positive robustness or impossibility of it is asserted. For n=1 logarithmic envelopes use their positive values at n=2, without changing the structured asymptotic forms.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
